paper_metadata.title: VaR Estimation with Quantum Computing Noise Correction Using Neural Networks

summary: The paper proposes a gate‑based quantum circuit that samples the tail of a Gaussian loss distribution to estimate portfolio VaR, demonstrated on a 138‑asset dataset. A 4‑qubit circuit was validated in simulation and executed on IBM Lagos, where noise distorted the distribution; a hybrid approach using a 3‑layer neural network to tune circuit rotations on a 5‑qubit device produced a VaR estimate of USD 1376 versus the classical parametric value of USD 1380 (<1% error). No computational speedup over classical Monte Carlo or parametric methods is demonstrated.

experiments.description: Quantum circuit for VaR estimation using a windowed Gaussian distribution, executed on a statevector simulator to validate the gate-based circuit design.

algorithm.variant: Qiskit state preparation for Gaussian-tail sampling in VaR estimation
algorithm.ansatz: state preparation circuit with uniformly controlled rotations

problem_formulation.encoding_details: Prepare a quantum state whose amplitudes approximate a clipped Gaussian distribution over a window mapped to 2^n basis states; 4 qubits used in the example.
problem_formulation.objective_function: Estimate the 1% VaR by sampling the tail of a Gaussian loss distribution and mapping the measured basis state to the VaR interval.
problem_formulation.constraints_handling: Windowing/clipping of the Gaussian tail to [-3σ, -2σ] and rescaling of the confidence level from α to β within the window.

problem_instance.description: VaR estimation for a portfolio of 138 assets from a Peruvian financial institution, using the linearized Gaussian-loss model to define the target distribution for the quantum circuit.

dataset_specification.description: Six months of asset data; historical series used to compute covariance/Cholesky and the Gaussian loss width σ.

problem_instance.data_preprocessing_details: Covariance matrix computed from asset series increments; Cholesky factorization via modified Cheng/Higham approach; linear approximation used to reduce the loss distribution to a single Gaussian variable; tail window restricted to [-3σ, -2σ].
problem_instance.evaluation_methodology: Statevector simulation of the circuit; VaR read from the measured basis-state probability and scaled back to the loss axis.

implementation_details.classical_preprocessing: Compute covariance and Cholesky matrices; derive σ and the windowed probability parameter β.
implementation_details.classical_postprocessing: Scale the measured basis state back to the VaR value on the loss axis.

speedup_claims.caveats: This is a proof-of-concept state-preparation circuit for VaR sampling; no quantum speedup is claimed or demonstrated.

advantage_assessment.resources_for_advantage: Not specified; the experiment only demonstrates circuit construction and sampling from a clipped Gaussian distribution using a 4‑qubit simulator.
limiting_factors: No runtime comparison with classical Monte Carlo
Quantum circuit used only for sampling a single Gaussian variable

notes: 4-qubit circuit is explicitly shown in Figure 5; statevector simulator is explicitly named.
Circuit depth not numerically reported; inferred as a multi-gate state-preparation circuit from the figure, but exact depth unavailable.
No asymptotic quantum speedup is claimed for this circuit; it is a proof-of-concept VaR sampler.
The simulator experiment validates circuit correctness but does not claim any computational advantage.
All heavy computations (covariance, Cholesky, σ calculation) remain classical.

problem_formulation.objective_function: Estimate the 1% VaR from the tail of the loss distribution.
problem_formulation.constraints_handling: Windowing/clipping of the Gaussian tail and rescaling of the confidence level within the window.

experiments.description: Hybrid neural-network-assisted calibration of qubit rotations to mitigate noise and improve VaR estimation on a real quantum computer.

algorithm.variant: classical neural network optimizing rotation parameters of a Qiskit quantum circuit
algorithm.ansatz: Qiskit state-preparation circuit with rotation gates and CNOTs; 3 dense-layer classical NN used for parameter prediction
algorithm.optimizer: neural-network training using Keras loss minimization

hyperparameters.cross_validation: leave-one-out style (all values except one for training, one for validation)

algorithm.parameter_initialization: Random initial qubit rotations / random neural-network weights at the first epoch

problem_formulation.encoding_details: Five-qubit circuit encodes a discretized VaR distribution over 32 basis states; neural network adjusts rotation angles to match the target VaR histogram.
problem_formulation.objective_function: Minimize the cost between quantum-estimated VaR and historical/parametric VaR by tuning qubit rotation angles.
problem_formulation.constraints_handling: Rotation angles constrained to the qubit rotation range [-π, π] via bounded activations (ReLU saturated at π or sigmoid mapped to [-π, π]).

problem_instance.description: Training/validation on a 5-asset dataset derived from the Peru financial data; target VaR around USD 1380.

dataset_specification.description: Five assets used for training due to hardware/time limits; cross-validation over grouped asset values.

problem_instance.data_preprocessing_details: Historical VaR computed for each grouped asset; training/validation split; minVaR and maxVaR define the distribution window; β computed from the windowed CDF.
problem_instance.evaluation_methodology: Neural-network training over grouped inputs; validation against target VaR; final real-hardware histogram used to read VaR 1376 USD.

hardware.device_name: IBM Quantum device (exact device not specified in Section 5.4)

noise_model.mitigation_details: Neural network learns qubit rotation parameters to compensate for noise; paper mentions executing circuits 1000 to 2000 times for valid statistics.

implementation_details.classical_preprocessing: Compute historical VaR, split grouped assets into training/validation, derive minVaR/maxVaR window and β.
implementation_details.classical_postprocessing: Compare quantum-estimated VaR to target/historical VaR; use the cost to update neural-network weights.

speedup_claims.caveats: The hybrid neural-network approach is presented as noise mitigation and calibration, not as a speedup method.

advantage_assessment.resources_for_advantage: Substantially larger fault‑tolerant quantum processors plus elimination of classical preprocessing would be required to outperform parametric VaR models.
limiting_factors: Hybrid classical neural network required for noise correction
No complexity or runtime advantage shown
Accuracy target derived from classical parametric VaR

notes: 5 qubits are explicitly stated for the real-hardware experiment.

The paper states that 1000 to 2000 executions are needed for valid statistics; num_shots recorded as 1000 as the lower bound explicitly mentioned, but the exact run count for the final experiment is not specified.
Exact circuit depth, gate counts, and optimizer details are not reported.
The corrected quantum estimate (USD 1376) is compared to the classical parametric VaR target (USD 1380), demonstrating similar accuracy but not superiority.
The authors explicitly state results are 'close enough' to classical methods.
